question: What is the main job of diagnostic devices in the hospital?

options.A: To detect, monitor, and evaluate physical conditions
options.B: To replace the physical assessment entirely
options.D: To manage hospital inventory and supplies

explanation: You've got this! Diagnostic devices are simply tools built to help healthcare workers spot health issues and keep an eye on how a patient is doing. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T1#GNS113_U4_T1_h1)

question: How does nursing informatics help us use digital diagnostic tools better?

options.A: By eliminating the need for routine vital signs
options.B: By streamlining data entry into electronic health records
options.C: By diagnosing patients without clinician input
options.D: By reducing the overall cost of medical equipment

explanation: Nursing informatics is all about making tech work for us! It helps patient test results flow smoothly straight into their digital records so nothing gets lost. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T1#GNS113_U4_T1_h1)

question: In medical imaging, what does the abbreviation PACS stand for?
explanation: Think of PACS as the digital filing cabinet where hospitals store and share all those important X-rays and scans! [learn more](GNS113_U4_T1#GNS113_U4_T1_h2)

question: Why is having a PACS system such a big win for hospital nursing units?

options.A: It allows multiple clinicians to view patient scans simultaneously
options.B: It prints physical films faster than traditional methods
options.C: It removes the need to verify patient identity before scans
options.D: It automatically generates final radiology reports for nurses

explanation: No more running around looking for physical films! With PACS, doctors and nurses on different wards can look at the same scan at the exact same time. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T1#GNS113_U4_T1_h2)

question: What kind of energy does an ultrasound machine use to snap its pictures?
explanation: Ultrasounds use safe sound waves that bounce off body tissues to create a live picture—just like bats use echo location! [learn more](GNS113_U4_T1#GNS113_U4_T1_h3)

question: A patient might have a full bladder and trouble passing urine, but you want to check them at the bedside without using radiation. What do you grab?
explanation: Spotting urine retention at the bedside is super easy and safe with a portable bladder ultrasound—no radiation involved at all! [learn more](GNS113_U4_T1#GNS113_U4_T1_h3)

question: What type of energy does a CT (computed tomography) scan rely on?
explanation: CT scans use clever X-ray beams that rotate around the patient to build super detailed 3D slices of the body. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T1#GNS113_U4_T1_h4)

question: Why do nurses always check for allergies before a patient has a CT scan with contrast dye?

options.A: To prevent severe allergic reactions to iodine-based contrast media
options.B: To check if the patient can safely lie flat for the procedure
options.C: To confirm the patient has fasted for at least twelve hours
options.D: To ensure the patient is not claustrophobic inside the machine

explanation: Some people have nasty allergic reactions to the iodine dye used to make CT images clearer. Always safety first! [learn more](GNS113_U4_T1#GNS113_U4_T1_h4)

question: Which of these imaging tests does NOT use dangerous ionizing radiation?
explanation: MRIs use powerful magnets and radio waves instead of radiation, making them safe from radiation exposure. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T1#GNS113_U4_T1_h5)

question: A patient booked for an MRI mentions they have a metal heart pacemaker. What is your most important immediate action as a nurse?

options.A: Cover the chest area with a lead apron during the scan
options.B: Notify the imaging department immediately to evaluate the device safety
options.C: Ask the patient to remove all clothing containing metal zippers
options.D: Administer a mild sedative to calm the patient inside the tube

explanation: Magnets and metal pacemakers do NOT mix! Always flag this to the imaging team right away to keep the patient safe. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T1#GNS113_U4_T1_h5)

question: What are the three golden rules of radiation safety when working around machines like X-rays?
explanation: Remember the big three: spend less time near the source, stay as far back as you can, and use lead shields! [learn more](GNS113_U4_T1#GNS113_U4_T1_h6)

question: Why is keeping diagnostic test results secure in a hospital computer network an ethical must?

options.A: To maintain patient confidentiality and privacy rights
options.B: To reduce the number of duplicate diagnostic orders
options.C: To prevent the hospital from paying regulatory fines
options.D: To ensure the equipment manufacturer updates their software

explanation: Patients trust us with their most private health data. Keeping their digital files secure is a core part of our duty as nurses. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T1#GNS113_U4_T1_h6)
